title: On‑Prem CP Commissioning and Rotation Scenarios (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures field‑operations style procedures for commissioning a private control plane (on‑prem or VPC) and execution patterns for key rotations and minor version upgrades. It is an operational draft intended to sit alongside module README and formal runbooks. Use this for day‑zero provisioning, small cluster scaleups, and rotation rehearsals.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, Platform Engineers deploying customer private control planes, Solutions engineers doing on‑site commissioning.
- Scope: initial infra provisioning using Terraform modules, minimal post‑install validation, scale‑up sequences for worker nodes and API planes, and key/service credential rotations. Not in scope: deep networking design for customer networks, full security assessment (see SEC playbooks).

Quick glossary (local shorthand used in notes):
- CP = private control plane (customer VPC / on‑prem bundle)
- Ops cluster = control plane hosts + management VMs (etcd, kubecontrol, operator)
- App cluster = runtime GPUs or dedicated inference pools (handled by Dedicated team)
- TF = Terraform modules in private-cp-terraform repo
- KMS = customer key management (HSM/KMS)

Prereqs (pre‑commission checklist):
- Customer networking: subnet ranges, NAT egress, firewall rules documented and confirmed (ticketed).
- DNS: wildcard A/ALIAS records or internal DNS delegation ready.
- KMS: KMS key provisioned and account/service principal added (or HSM connection details).
- Service accounts: idempotent service principals created and key artifacts staged in secure vault (HashiCorp Vault or SSM).
- Terraform access: operator has TF Cloud or GitHub Actions creds and backend bucket for state locking configured.
- Image/artifact registry access: registry credentials validated.
- Capacity plan: initial node counts, machine types, and expected peak qps.
- ACLs: RBAC mapping spreadsheet shared with customer.

Module notes and conventions (TF):
- Module naming: modules/private-cp/* with submodules for network, controlplane, kms-bindings, and bootstrap-ops. Keep naming stable across minors.
- State layout: one state per environment (customer-<org>-<env>). Avoid mixing control plane + app cluster in one state for easier rollback.
- Variables: prefer explicit lists to count-based scaling (nodes = list of objects). This reduces surprises during apply.
- Immutable tags: tag resources with: customer, cp-version, tf-state-id.
- Rollback pattern: use TF plan + selective apply targeting module paths (e.g., module.controlplane) not the whole state unless necessary.
- Sensitive outputs: do not export private keys; write secrets to Vault or SOPS file and reference externally.

Commissioning sequence (preferred, minimal safe path):
1) Preflight verification (local): run network checks (ping to endpoints, port checks for 443, 2379 for etcd if exposed internally), validate DNS entries resolve to intended subnets.
2) Terraform init + plan in dry run mode; create plan artifact and upload to ticket thread.
3) Apply networking module only (create VPC subnets, route tables, security groups). Validate with simple probes.
4) Apply KMS bindings module: ensure service principal has encrypt/decrypt permissions. Validate with a test encryption/decryption run using the same SA.
5) Apply controlplane module with minimum replicas (master=3 recommended) and bootstrap operator enabled.
6) Wait for operator to finish reconciliation. Validate pods, CRDs, and sanity endpoints: /health, control plane metrics, etcd cluster status.
7) Smoke test: issue a simple inference request to hosted edge (if available) or run integration test harness (link in artifacts).
8) Snapshot state and register a version tag in the control plane metadata (used for upgrades later).

Validation checklist (post apply):
- etcd: cluster healthy, status OK, no member mismatch.
- Kubernetes API: <250ms median for simple GET requests from internal probe.
- Controlplane pods: desired replicas match and RollingRestart count is zero.
- Logs: no panic/segfaults in operator or core services.
- Metrics: heartbeats from agents in last 2m.
- Backup test: run etcd snapshot to object store (verify restore dry run).
- Security test: KMS test encryption/decryption log shows SA usage.

Scaling patterns (small increments safe to run manually):
- Horizontal control plane scale (adding management workers): update TF module variable workers = append([...]). Use plan, then apply module only. Expect brief API surface fluctuation; probe readiness until stable.
- Vertical changes (machine type upsizes): create new instance group with larger type, cordon + drain old nodes, then decommission. Avoid in‑place instance type changes unless using immutable groups.
- Burst capacity for scheduling GPUs: prefer autoscaler policies at app cluster level. CP should remain small and stable.
- Batching of control plane changes: group innocuous changes (tags, noncritical labels) separately from scaling and security changes to reduce blast radius.

Rotation procedures (KMS keys, SA keys, TLS certs):
- Principle: rehearse rotations during a maintenance window with a canary subset first. Keep one read-only copy of the old key until validation complete.

KMS key rotation (customer-managed):
1) Confirm current key arn and rotation policy.
2) Create new key version (or new key if HSM) and grant same bindings.
3) Update TF variable kms_key_id to new value in a feature branch, plan and apply only kms module.
4) Run key‑swap script that updates service principal secrets to reference new key.
5) Validate by performing encrypt/decrypt tests and smoke inference with stored secrets.
6) After 48‑72 hours of stable traffic, schedule depublish of old key (move to disabled state) then schedule deletion per customer policy.

Service account (SA) key rotation:
- Preferred flow: generate new SA key, store in Vault, roll consumer deployments to read new secret, then revoke old key.
- Rolling strategy: annotate deployments with secret version label and perform a controlled rollout via operator. Validate connectivity after each batch.

TLS cert rotation (controlplane endpoints):
- Use short TTL certs behind automated renewal (cert-manager or equivalent). For manual: stage cert on alternate listener, shift traffic, then decommission old cert.

Upgrade plan (minor version upgrades, non‑major):
- Prechecks: ensure snapshot/backups completed, plan artifact saved, smoke tests passing.
- Canary: pick one controlplane replica (or a single customer region) and perform the full upgrade there using TF module version bump or image tag change. Validate for 6–12 hours.
- Gradual roll: upgrade remaining replicas in rolling fashion with pause and validation gates between each.
- Auto rollback: if operator reports critical errors or API median latency >2x baseline for 30m, trigger rollback using saved snapshot and TF rollback plan.
- Post‑upgrade: run regression evals on a curated prompt set (link test harness in artifacts) to check inference correctness with new runtime changes.

Emergency evacuation (short notes):
- If a control plane becomes unrecoverable, follow these steps:
  1) Cut network access to the failing CP to avoid split brain.
  2) Restore latest etcd snapshot into a fresh controlplane state in an isolated maintenance VPC.
  3) Recreate TF state in a recovery bucket (use new state id) and import resources where necessary.
  4) Re-attach app clusters by updating routing/ingress to new CP endpoints.
- Post‑evacuation: open incident ticket and schedule full post‑mortem with timeline and TF diffs attached.

Testing and rehearsal notes (important):
- Run quarterly rotation rehearsals in staging with simulated production traffic. Log time required for full KMS rotation, SA rotation, and restore.
- Maintain a public deck with expected MTR (mean time to rotate) metrics for customer SLAs.
- TODO: add automated playbook runner (ansible + small CLI) to encapsulate common steps above.

Operational hygiene and followups:
- Tag every apply with ticket ID and operator username.
- Keep TF plan artifacts for at least 30 days per customer.
- Maintain a short audit note in the CP metadata after any rotation or upgrade: who, what, rollback id, notes.
- If making sensitive changes (KMS or certs), run a secondary reviewer approval in PR and a post‑change verification runbook.

Open questions / TODOs (work in progress):
- Should we standardize on a single SA rotation tool across customers or ship a small SNOMAD utility? (discuss in eng private deploys sync)
- Define exact SLOs to trigger automatic rollback on upgrades (latency thresholds + error budget consumption).
- Add step‑by‑step screenshots or CLI examples for Terraform apply workloads.

Ownership and escalation contacts:
- Oncall CP eng: james.liu@redwood.com (primary)
- Private deployments lead: aisha.patel@redwood.com
- Security contact (KMS/HSM): marisol.gomez@redwood.com
- SRE escalation (pager): #sre-pager (Slack)

Appendix A — quick CLI snippets (examples to copy into operator shell):
- TF plan with out file: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan -var-file=customer.tfvars
- Apply network module only: terraform apply -target=module.network plan.tfplan
- etcd snapshot: RUST_LOG=info ./ctl snapshot save --bucket s3://backups-cp/customerX --name pre-upgrade-2026-02-17

Appendix B — post‑change verification checklist (short):
- 5m: all pods up, no CrashLoopBackOff
- 30m: metric baselines within 10%
- 2h: smoke evals pass
- 48h: KMS key usage normal, no errors

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short and link to module READMEs. Add concrete TF variable examples next edit.
- Capture a short automation sprint to reduce manual steps for kms rotations.

End of draft.
